text: Single-click a cell to cycle
why: Rev 14 removed single-click status cycling because it WAS the OMS-003 defect: a double-click fires two single clicks first, so following the instruction advanced status twice across 84 live cells. The tooltip kept teaching it for eleven revisions.

text: Single click a month cell to cycle
why: Same claim in the User Guide, which for eleven revisions contradicted its own troubleshooting section on the same page.

text: User must set a new password on next login
why: The Admin Console promised this while writing a plaintext value that authentication never read. The control was deleted in Rev 29; the promise must not return without something behind it. The binding was tightened on 6 Sept 2026: it named the bare identifier, which the Rev 29 comment recording the deletion also contains, so the guard was satisfied by the note explaining that nothing implements it. Binding values must be code-shaped - the code search covers comments and the revision log too.

text: and initial password.
why: The add-user tooltip listed a password field that had been removed, on a form that creates a directory entry rather than a sign-in account. Rev 32 restored the field and made it real: the binding now proves the promise is kept rather than that it was withdrawn.

requires_text: category
why: Rev 23 gave tasks a category. The Add and Edit tooltips went on listing the old field set for two revisions.

requires_text: waiting on
why: Rev 24 added a prerequisite field. Same omission as the category.

requires_text: end date
why: Rev 17 added End Date and End Time. The Add Event tooltip described neither until Rev 29.

requires_text: Tick Standing for anything that repeats
why: Rev 17 added the recurring flag; nothing described it. Rev 53 (R-13) renamed the user-facing word: the same bit was called Cadence on the Add Event tooltip, Recurring on the event form and Standing on the calendar chips, on adjacent screens. The stored field is still `recurring` - only the word people read changed - so the binding still guards the control and now guards the agreed word with it.

requires_text: every event, task AND SOP
why: Rev 23 made renaming a category move tasks too. The tooltip still said it updated every event, understating the blast radius of a merge. Rev 54 (R-04) added the SOP loop and repointed this at the wider sentence; the tasks loop it guards is unchanged.

requires_text: checklist
why: A control users cannot find is a control that was not built. Rev 41 added reachable_from: existence is not reachability, and this binding passed at Rev 34 while the control it guards was on one form out of two.

requires_text: due in the next three days
why: The reminder horizon is a promise about behaviour and must match the code that implements it. Rev 41 added reachable_from: existence is not reachability, and this binding passed at Rev 34 while the control it guards was on one form out of two.

requires_text: Sort any column
why: Rev 23 made every column sortable and said so nowhere until Rev 29. Rev 41 added reachable_from: existence is not reachability, and this binding passed at Rev 34 while the control it guards was on one form out of two.

requires_text: Blocked
why: A status a user will see on screen has to be explained somewhere.

requires_text: change it before they can use OMS
why: Initial passwords are guessable by design, so the forced change is the control that makes them safe. If it is ever removed, the text promising it must go at the same time.

requires_text: Disable sign-in
why: Rev 30 made deactivation block sign-in. Before that it flipped a directory flag only, which read as revoked access and was not. Rev 41 added reachable_from: existence is not reachability, and this binding passed at Rev 34 while the control it guards was on one form out of two.

requires_text: Retired
why: Rev 17 added a status that changes how completion is counted. It must stay explained.

requires_text: Unsynced
why: The id-less-record guard surfaces a state the user has to act on. If the guard exists, the guide must say what the state means.

requires_text: Add User creates both
why: Rev 32 made Add User create a sign-in as well as a directory entry. The form's own note had claimed the opposite for an hour after Rev 30 made it false.

text: This does NOT create a sign-in account
why: The Add User button's own tooltip, and the third stale claim found in one day. It was true until Rev 32 put a sign-in checkbox on the very form it describes. Nothing tied the button's description to the form's fields, so it would have gone on telling administrators the opposite of what the button does.

text: Sign-in accounts are issued separately, through the gateway
why: True until Rev 30 gave the client an account-creation path. The claim must not return while that path exists.

requires_text: OMS reads the event name and works the category out
why: Rev 33 made the importer derive a category when the workbook column is blank - 145 of Ari's 182 rows. If that derivation is ever removed, the guide promising it must go at the same time, or the calendar silently fills with Other again while the text says otherwise. Rev 41 added reachable_from: existence is not reachability, and this binding passed at Rev 34 while the control it guards was on one form out of two.

requires_text: The workbook’s wording is translated, not copied
why: The alias table is the only thing stopping 'School of Medicine Events' appearing beside 'SOM Events' the moment the workbook column is filled in. It is invisible when working, so nothing but this binding would notice it being dropped.

requires_text: OMS has one read tier
why: Bound to the client's access-level helper because check 12 only reads oms.html. Writes are enforced at the gateway but reads are not segmented: every signed-in account receives all of canonical state. Users will assume read-only means restricted visibility unless told plainly, and that assumption is how something confidential ends up in a note.

requires_text: Standing only
why: OMS-041. A filter nobody can find is a filter that was not built, and this one reuses an existing field rather than adding a visible one, so nothing else hints it exists.

requires_text: SOPs have a review date
why: OMS-028. The review date drives an Overdue flag on a Dean-facing table; if the field is ever dropped the promise must go with it. Rev 41 added reachable_from: existence is not reachability, and this binding passed at Rev 34 while the control it guards was on one form out of two.

requires_text: Nothing fills this in for you
why: OMS-041. The checkbox is the ONLY way cadence is ever set, and both places that described it said the opposite - the form hint said 'The Outlook sync populates this field' and the guide said 'The Outlook calendar sync fills this in automatically'. There is no Outlook calendar sync; the app's own notification callout says the Outlook integration is a mailto draft precisely to avoid Graph. Text telling users a field fills itself is why 248 of 255 events carry no cadence at all.

requires_text: Events and SOPs retire the same way
why: OMS-049 and OMS-028. The guide promises retirement on BOTH forms in one unscoped sentence, which is precisely the shape that let Rev 34 ship the attributed-note control on one dialog out of two while check 12 passed. reachable_from names both forms so the sentence cannot outlive either control.

requires_text: drops out of the 30-day count and the Weekly Brief
why: OMS-049. Retiring a record is only meaningful if it leaves the numbers people decide from; a Retired event still counted would be worse than deleting it, because the count would be quietly wrong rather than visibly short. The binding is the filter expression itself, so dropping it from either surface fails.

requires_text: it stays on the calendar marked Retired
why: OMS-049. Retiring must not read as deleting, so the record has to remain on screen wearing the label. Grid and list are separate render paths - Rev 34 shipped a control on one surface out of two and check 12 passed - so both builders are named.

requires_text: chosen from the same list events and tasks use
why: OMS-028, DEC-022. The whole decision was to reuse the existing vocabulary rather than invent an SOP taxonomy. If the control is ever repointed at a private list the sentence promising a shared one has to go with it.

requires_text: a category invented on an SOP is offered everywhere
why: OMS-028. eventCategories derives the list from the records that use it, so a collection left out loses its categories the moment nothing else uses them - the exact bug the Rev 23 comment records for tasks. SOPs had to be added for the same reason, and this binds the promise to the code that keeps it.

requires_text: carried forward
why: OMS-041. Before Rev 48 a source replacement rebuilt every row from the workbook, so cadence ticked by hand was erased by the next import and nothing said so. Both the Event form and the guide now promise it survives; reachable_from names the preview AND confirmImport because a promise that holds on screen but not at the write path is the worse half to lose.

requires_text: import preview shows what it worked out
why: OMS-041. Deriving cadence from a title is inference, and the standing posture for inference in this importer is crossSourceDuplicates: report it, require confirmation, never resolve silently. The toggle is what makes the derived value a proposal rather than a decision, so if it stops being reachable from the preview the text promising it must go too.

requires_text: The sheet must state its year
why: Rev 53 (B-05). parseKeyDateLead hard-coded `colIndex<12?2026:2027`, so the 2028 workbook would have imported silently into 2026 and 2027 and nothing anywhere would have said so. The year now comes from the sheet, and a sheet that states none is refused rather than guessed at. The refusal is only defensible if the interface says the rule beforehand, so the upload card carries it; if the derivation is ever removed the sentence has to go in the same change. reachable_from names the parser because a derivation nothing calls is the Rev 34 shape all over again.

requires_text: keeps that event
why: Rev 53 (B-03, B-11, R-02). confirmImport rebuilt every row with a fresh uid(), so a re-import broke every task.sourceEventId link, un-retired Retired events and erased End Date and End Time set by hand. A matched row now keeps the event it matches. Three surfaces promise it - the upload card, the preview callout and the guide - and all three are false the moment the lookup stops being reached, so the preview, the write path and the cadence resolver are all named.

requires_text: loses its source-event link
why: Rev 53 (B-03). The prompt used to say 'Tasks and all non-calendar data will remain unchanged', which was true of the Tasks collection and untrue of the links out of it: a task pointing at an event no incoming row matched was left pointing at a record that had just been deleted. The count is now on screen before anybody types REPLACE. A promise about a number nobody computes is worse than no promise, so both the preview and the write path are named.

requires_text: typed out a second time with both numbers
why: Rev 53 (B-10). Only the Key Dates path had a size gate. A workbook saved with one sheet, or whose sheet names changed, arrives as a handful of rows and deletes the rest of that owner's calendar without a word. The guard exists now; the guide describes it; neither is any use alone. reachable_from names confirmImport because the guard is worth nothing sitting beside the write path instead of in front of it.

requires_text: the date cell could not be read
why: Rev 53 (B-06). The string branches of xlSerialToDate were unanchored and split the whole cell, so '13/45/2026' became '2026-13-45' and rendered NaN on a Dean-facing calendar. Such a cell is refused now, and a refusal nobody is told about is indistinguishable from a row the workbook never had - so the count is shown in the preview. If the counter goes, the sentence promising the count must go with it.

requires_text: Daily, Weekly, Bi-weekly, Monthly, Bi-monthly, Quarterly, Semi-annual, Standing or Recurring
why: Rev 53 (R-08). The regex matched seven words and the guide listed four, in the one place a reader checks what the importer is about to decide for them. The binding is the alternation itself, so adding or removing a word fails until the sentence is updated in the same change. Annual stays out of both by decision: on the live workbook every annual match is a once-a-year event, which is exactly what the standing chip must not catch.

requires_text: shows a Standing column
why: Rev 53 (R-13). The same bit was called Cadence in the import preview, Recurring on the event form and Standing on the calendar chips - three words for one boolean on adjacent screens. The guide now names the column, so the column and the sentence naming it fail together.

text: No Task and no non-calendar collection is modified
why: Rev 53 (B-08, B-09). The claim is the strongest sentence the importer makes, and until Rev 53 the code behind it did not support it in either direction: _dirty.clear() discarded pending unsent work in every other collection, and the verification compared collections that nothing between the snapshot and the comparison could have touched. The sentence may only stand while the check does.

text: Replacement was not saved
why: Rev 53 (B-09). The alert said the replacement was not saved and there was no code that could unsay it: the guard could not fail, and had it failed it had no way back. The sentence is allowed only while a rollback exists. Do not satisfy this with an empty restore - the smoke suite asserts that the snapshot really does put every collection back.

text: sync populates this field
why: OMS-041 tripwire. This sentence was in the artifact for two revisions with nothing behind it. If anybody writes it again, the gate now demands a symbol that will only exist once a calendar sync is actually built. Do not satisfy this by defining an empty OMS_OUTLOOK_SYNC - delete the claim instead.

text: fills this in automatically
why: OMS-041 tripwire, guide wording of the same false claim. Paired with no-calendar-sync-may-be-claimed because the two sentences drifted independently, in two files' worth of prose, saying the same untrue thing.

requires_text: SOP Reviews Due
why: OMS-047. The card is the only place a lapsed SOP review is visible to somebody who is not already on the SOPs tab, and the guide now promises it on the Dashboard. reachable_from names rDash because that promise is what an orphan would silently break.

requires_text: due within the next 30 days
why: OMS-047, and the reason this binding exists at all. sopsDueSoon shipped in Rev 34 and was called from NOWHERE until Rev 46: dead code behind a described feature. The whole gate missed it - the smoke suite asserted only that it was defined, which an orphan satisfies, and check 12 was watching sopReviewCell instead. Chaining reachable_from to sopReviewCard, which is itself chained to rDash, is what makes the next orphan at either level fail.

requires_text: Searching SOPs reads the notes too
why: OMS-028. The SOPs table renders notes in a column of their own, so a search that does not read them fails on a word the user can see on screen. If the haystack is ever narrowed back to process and owner, the sentence promising otherwise has to go with it.

requires_text: Notes are added to, not typed over
why: OMS-015. This is the whole answer to comments-versus-notes. Users must know an appended note is attributed, or they will keep retyping the box and overwriting each other, which is the defect it fixes. Rev 41 added reachable_from: existence is not reachability, and this binding passed at Rev 34 while the control it guards was on one form out of two.

requires_text: Log a call or an email OMS did not send
why: OMS-029. The control sits inside the Notification Queue modal, which most people open only to send a draft, so it is easy to miss and needs describing. Rev 41 added reachable_from: existence is not reachability, and this binding passed at Rev 34 while the control it guards was on one form out of two.

requires_text: OMS keeps checking every few seconds until it does
why: Rev 35. Users were told to wait and not reload while nothing was checking, so a save that had already landed looked stuck. If the reconciler is ever removed, the promise that it recovers on its own must go with it, or the guide becomes an instruction to wait forever. Rev 41 added reachable_from: existence is not reachability, and this binding passed at Rev 34 while the control it guards was on one form out of two.

requires_text: Out-of-office entries are hidden by default
why: Rev 35 hides fifteen existing calendar rows. Hiding data without saying so is how people conclude the calendar is wrong.

requires_text: holds what you asked for
why: Rev 36. Confirmation used to be a bare revision increase, and consolidate.py bumps the revision once per batch INCLUDING rejected operations - so a colleague's save, or an outright rejection, was reported to the user as 'Save successful' while their edit reverted on screen. If this predicate is ever removed the promise that confirmation means the change is really there must go with it, or the interface returns to certifying saves that did not happen. Rev 41 added reachable_from: existence is not reachability, and this binding passed at Rev 34 while the control it guards was on one form out of two.

requires_text: did not reach shared OMS
why: Rev 36. Two different situations wore one banner: operations accepted by the gateway and awaiting the fold, where waiting works and reloading is harmless, and operations that never left the browser, where waiting does nothing and reloading DISCARDS the edit. The guide can only tell people what to do if the banner distinguishes them, so the branch and the text stand or fall together.

requires_text: it waits, and your next save carries everything
why: Rev 36. Adoption replaces ST wholesale, so the reconciler must not run it over something typed since the operations went to the gateway. The guide promises exactly that. The old guard tested _dirty, which cannot tell an unsent edit from an unconfirmed one and was the reason the reconciler never fired at all.

requires_text: is not sent twice
why: Rev 37. OMS_BASE advances only on a confirmed sync, so before this a second save recomputed the diff against the same stale base and re-sent the whole outstanding batch. On 5 Sept one ten-operation batch went to the gateway three times in forty-one seconds with identical payloads, which is 51 of the 53 records in conflicts/unresolved. If the suppression is ever removed the guide must stop promising it, or the conflict log fills with noise again and the one place a genuinely lost edit would show becomes unreadable. Rev 41 added reachable_from: existence is not reachability, and this binding passed at Rev 34 while the control it guards was on one form out of two.

requires_text: now carries an identifier of its own
why: Rev 38. Add Workstream pushed a rob row with no id for three revisions after the 5 Sept 2026 migration cleared exactly that condition out of the data. OMS_MAP keeps a record only when id != null and both sides of the sync diff use it, so the row emitted no operation in any direction. If the id assignment is ever dropped, the guide sentence promising the row reaches the shared record has to go with it - and the general push-site sweep in smoke.mjs should fail first. Rev 41 added reachable_from: existence is not reachability, and this binding passed at Rev 34 while the control it guards was on one form out of two.

requires_text: The checking slows down, it does not stop
why: Rev 39. Every reconciler tick is one /api/state, which is one GitHub contents read against an installation limit of 5,000 an hour that is shared with sign-in, every save and the consolidator's own pushes. Rev 36 made the reconciler fire for the first time and its flat three-second poll became 1,200 reads an hour per stuck client, uncapped - four of them would have taken the whole system down in a way that would not have looked like polling. The backoff is what makes an indefinite watch affordable, so if it is ever removed the promise that OMS keeps watching has to be re-examined rather than silently made expensive again. Rev 41 added reachable_from: existence is not reachability, and this binding passed at Rev 34 while the control it guards was on one form out of two.

requires_text: It ends a session that is already open, within about a minute
why: Rev 42, correcting Rev 40. requireSession once returned the role FROM THE TOKEN and never read auth/users.json, so disabling somebody changed nothing for up to eight hours. Rev 40 wrote that limitation into the guide truthfully - and gateway OMS-051 removed it the same afternoon, which made the sentence false and left check 12 REQUIRING a false claim. That is the standing instruction's own failure mode running backwards, and it happened because check 12 reads only oms.html and cannot see the gateway. Bound to the client's session accessor for the same reason. If per-request resolution is ever removed at the gateway, this sentence has to be revisited in the same change.

requires_text: A refused save now says why
why: Rev 41. OMS_POST reported EVERY 403 as auth:true, so a read-only account trying to save was told its session had expired - false, and signing in again would have changed nothing. If the branch is ever collapsed back into a single 403 case, the guide sentence promising a specific reason has to go with it.

requires_text: sign out and sign in again
why: Rev 41 / gateway OMS-053. The forced password change is now refused at the write path rather than only by the client, and the control that clears it lives on the sign-in page, not inside the application. Somebody already signed in therefore has to sign out and back in, and the guide is the only place that says so. If enforcement is ever removed, this instruction must go too - it would be telling people to do something with no purpose.

requires_text: Other people's changes arrive on their own
why: Rev 44. Before this the client fetched shared state only at sign-in, during a save, and while the reconciler ran; an hour idle on a Connected session made zero calls and the screen stayed stale until you saved. If the watch is ever removed, the sentence promising that a colleague's work appears has to go with it - and reachable_from is on OMS_BOOT because a watch that is defined but never started is exactly the Rev 35 reconciler again.

requires_text: as long as they touch different fields
why: Rev 44. An update used to send the whole record, so every key overlapped and consolidate.py raised a same-field conflict for ANY two edits to one record - reproduced: A edits the title, B edits the notes, B is rejected and B's note is gone. If this ever reverts to sending the whole record the guide must stop promising concurrent edits work, because they will not.

requires_text: the one piece of code OMS loads from anywhere but itself
why: Rev 45. SheetJS is the only external script, it runs with full access to the page including the session token in sessionStorage, and it was loaded with no integrity attribute - so a compromise of that CDN or of DNS in front of it would have read every signed-in user's credential silently. If the pin is ever dropped, the sentence saying the spreadsheet reader is verified must go with it. Recompute the hash when the version changes; the browser refuses to run anything that does not match.

text: is kept and sent as soon as that one lands
why: Rev 50. The guide had said 'the first one is not lost', which was true, while a DIFFERENT edit made during confirmation was overwritten by wholesale adoption and reported as Save successful. The sentence now promises the replay; this binds it to the function that performs it.

requires_text: everything else in the same save still goes through
why: Rev 50. Existence is not reachability: the replay has to run on the confirmed-save path AND the conflict path, or one of them still discards work. Orphan it from either and this fails.

text: as long as they touch different fields
why: Rev 44 wrote this sentence while OMS_ASSERT_CURRENT refused any update whose record version had moved at all, so the consolidator's field-level merge was unreachable in the ordinary case. This binds the promise to the rebase that makes it true.

text: looks for new shared work about once a minute
why: Rev 44's idle refresh was blocked for the life of every session by the boot migration's save() leaving all collections dirty. Live-verified 6 Sept 2026. The promise is only true with this guard in the boot sequence.

text: Links are checked before they are followed
why: Rev 51. Stored links were rendered straight into href with no scheme check. The guide now says links are checked; this binds the sentence to the check.

requires_text: or mailto link
why: Rev 51. Existence is not reachability: a link filter that one renderer skips is not a link filter. Every renderer that draws a stored link is named here.

text: Sign Out removes that copy along with the session
why: Rev 51. Sign-out left the whole shared state in localStorage. The guide now promises it is removed; this binds the promise to the removal.

text: Your role is confirmed with the gateway at sign-in
why: Rev 51. The role used to be read only from a sessionStorage blob written by the sign-in page. The guide now says the gateway confirms it; this binds that to the call.

text: The middle part is random, so a name does not determine a password
why: Rev 51 (E-01). The generator returned surname plus a fixed suffix, in a public file. The hint now says the middle is random; this binds it to the generator.

requires_text: sign-in account included
why: Rev 52 (A-03). omsRemoveSignIn was defined in Rev 30 and called from nowhere for twenty revisions while the Delete confirm said the user was removed completely. Existence is not reachability.

text: Set access levels: admin
why: Rev 52 (A-01, D-01). The nav tooltip promised access levels while the control wrote a directory field the gateway never read. The gateway gained a role action in OMS-063; this binds the promise to the call.

requires_text: changes the level their sign-in account is enforced at
why: Rev 52. The role call has to sit on the Edit User save path, or the dropdown is decoration again.

text: blocks their sign-in
why: Rev 52 (A-02). The tooltip said the person would lose access on next login while the function set a flag authentication never read. The Rev 30 comment above omsToggleSignIn called that exact trap out and left it in place.

requires_text: Deactivate blocks
why: Rev 52. The block has to happen on the Deactivate button's own path, not only on the separate Disable sign-in control.

requires_text: every event, task AND SOP
why: R-04. SOPs joined the shared category list in Rev 49 and renameCategory did not follow, so a category used only by procedures reported 'No records changed' and every SOP on it was stranded on a name nothing offered. The binding is the loop itself, in the same shape as the tasks one, so removing it from either side fails.

requires_text: shows all three counts before you confirm
why: A-12. Counting is only useful where the decision is made. The dialog shows the three counts and the confirmation quotes them, so this must be reachable from the render AND from the save that asks.

text: A task can be left (unassigned).
why: A-06. The Owner list had no empty entry, so a new task opened pre-assigned to whoever sorted first and saving it queued a notification telling them so. The guide may promise (unassigned) only while the option exists.

requires_text: nobody is emailed, until you choose them
why: A-06. The other half: an empty owner must not send the directory looking for a person, or the save prompts for an email address for nobody.

text: Two tasks cannot wait on each other.
why: A-17. Rev 24's comment called a cycle structurally impossible. It was creatable in two saves and left both tasks Blocked for ever. The guide may state the refusal only while the refusal is there.

requires_text: Retiring a prerequisite releases whatever was waiting on it
why: A-18. isBlocked has treated Retired as closed since Rev 24, but only Complete fired the handoff, so retiring a prerequisite unblocked its dependents silently. The wording has to say withdrawn rather than complete, because the reader acts on them differently.

requires_text: unsent reminders
why: A-10. A pending reminder addressed to the previous owner drafts an email telling somebody to finish work that is no longer theirs. Retiring those is only correct if it happens on the save that reassigns, hence reachable_from.

text: marked with a Retired badge
why: R-10. The Status hint and two guide lines said a Retired record is shown 'struck through'. Only .bret carries the line-through; the row never did. The claim is now tied to the badge that is actually drawn.

requires_text: drops out of the counts on the Dashboard, the Calendars and the Weekly Brief
why: A-19. The calendar pill and the list row divided by a total that included Retired work, so retiring made an event look LESS complete - the opposite of what the Status control promises.

text: the Standing only and Out of office filters
why: C-05. A calendar view saved three of the five filters on screen. Applying it reproduced the source and layout and quietly showed everything, which looks like it worked.

requires_text: the filter and the Status box on the form are drawn from one list
why: C-11. OMS_TASK_STATUSES was declared in Rev 17 and read by nothing; the chips and the form each carried their own copy, which is how a status comes to exist on one and not the other.

requires_text: review due date
why: R-11. The Add and Edit SOP tooltips listed title, owner, link and notes - the field set as it stood before Rev 46 added Review due and Rev 49 added Category and Status. Same drift the task tooltips had, three revisions of it.

requires_text: category, status, link
why: R-11. Retirement reached the SOP form in Rev 49 and no tooltip mentioned it, so the control existed and nothing pointed at it.

text: the status set here is the status the row keeps
why: A-08. Incoming, For Review, Board Commitments and Upcoming Deadlines are create-only: Rev 54 adds Delete but no edit dialog, so the form must stop implying the status can be moved on later. The claim is bound to the delete control that makes 'delete and re-add' actually possible.

requires_text: delete the row and add it again
why: A-08. A control on a card nobody renders is the Rev 34 shape all over again; the delete must be inside abSec, which is what draws all four sections.
